
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)

Retrieval Augmented Generation is a technique that combines information retrieval with large language models. Instead of relying entirely on the knowledge stored in an LLM during training, RAG retrieves relevant information from an external knowledge source and provides it as context to the LLM. This helps the model answer questions using specific and potentially updated information.

Document Chunking

Document chunking is the process of splitting large documents into smaller pieces called chunks. Embedding models have input token limits, so processing an entire large document at once may not be practical. Smaller chunks also allow the retrieval system to identify specific portions of a document rather than retrieving the entire document. Chunk size and overlap can significantly affect retrieval quality.

Text Embeddings

Text embeddings are numerical representations of text generated by embedding models. These representations capture semantic and contextual relationships between text passages. Semantically similar sentences tend to have vectors that are close to each other in the embedding space. Embeddings allow retrieval systems to search based on meaning rather than relying only on exact keyword matches.

Vector Databases

Vector databases are specialized systems designed to store and search high-dimensional vectors. They store embeddings along with associated identifiers, original text or references, and metadata. Examples include ChromaDB, Pinecone, Qdrant and Weaviate. Vector databases use similarity search and indexing techniques to efficiently retrieve relevant vectors.

Semantic Search

Semantic search retrieves information based on the meaning of a query rather than simply matching individual words. A query is converted into an embedding using the same embedding model used for document chunks. The query vector is compared with stored vectors using similarity measures such as cosine similarity. The most similar vectors are selected for retrieval.

Cosine Similarity

Cosine similarity measures the similarity between two vectors by calculating the cosine of the angle between them. Its value ranges from -1 to 1 mathematically, although embedding models and normalization choices influence the practical distribution of scores. Higher cosine similarity generally indicates greater semantic similarity. It is commonly used in semantic search systems.

Retrieval in RAG

The retrieval stage takes a user query and searches the vector database for relevant document chunks. The query is converted into an embedding, and the database finds the nearest vectors. A retrieval system often selects the top K most similar chunks. These chunks are then passed to the generation model as additional context.

Metadata Filtering

Metadata filtering allows a retrieval system to restrict its search to documents satisfying specific conditions. Metadata may include document names, authors, categories, dates and page numbers. For example, a system can retrieve information only from documents belonging to a particular category. Metadata filtering can be combined with vector similarity search.

Limitations of RAG

RAG systems can retrieve irrelevant or incomplete information. Poor chunking, weak embeddings and ambiguous queries can reduce retrieval quality. Even when relevant documents are retrieved, an LLM may misunderstand the context or generate unsupported information. Techniques such as reranking, query rewriting, hybrid search and retrieval evaluation can help improve system performance.
